# 5a. Statistical testing on the cell level

**Module 05a — Statistical testing on the cell level.** Differential abundance, clustering, and colocalization tests. Each test is a cell-level Wilcoxon comparison (cells are pooled by `condition`). Skip this module if you do not need formal comparisons or if you only want to use biological replicates.

With many cells these cell-level tests can overstate significance, because each cell is treated as an independent observation. When you have biological replicates (≥2 `sample_alias` values per `condition`), it can be a good idea to use `modules/05b_statistical_testing_pseudobulk.qmd` instead to increase reproducibility. The outputs from this notebook go under `{modality}/cell_level/`. 

```{r}
#| label: module05a_setup

library(here)
here::i_am("modules/05a_statistical_testing_cell_level.qmd")

source(here::here("modules", "common_setup.R"))

if (!exists("pg_data", inherits = TRUE)) {
  pg_data <- load_checkpoint("annotated_seurat_object.rds")
}
if (!exists("markers_to_test", inherits = TRUE)) {
  markers_to_test <- load_checkpoint("markers_to_test.rds")
}
```

## 5.0. Set Up Statistical Testing

> **Decision checkpoint** (statistical contrasts and plot cutoffs)  
> Set `contrast_column` and `reference_condition` (a value in that column). All `{target}_vs_{reference}` outputs in this notebook use this baseline. Adjust the significance and effect-size cutoffs used for summary plots. Result tables (`.rds` and `.csv`) are saved in full regardless of plot cutoffs.

By default, in this analysis we compare all conditions to a reference condition, which is typically a "resting", "untreated", or "control" condition. This allows us to identify markers that are differentially abundant or spatially clustered or colocalized in stimulated or treated conditions compared to the baseline state.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_set_reference

# Column in the Seurat object defining the groups to compare.
contrast_column <- "condition"

# Baseline / control condition. Must match a value in contrast_column.
# All tests compare each other condition against this one (target − reference).
# Output folders are named {target}_vs_{reference}.
reference_condition <- "resting"

# Summary-plot cutoffs. Volcano labels are the top n features by adjusted
# significance. These do not filter the saved result tables.
dabund_plot_p_adj_threshold <- 0.05
dabund_heatmap_effect_threshold <- 0.5
dabund_volcano_top_n <- 5

dclust_plot_p_adj_threshold <- 0.05
dclust_heatmap_effect_threshold <- 0.5
dclust_volcano_top_n <- 5

# Same effect-heatmap rule as abundance and clustering.
dcoloc_plot_p_adj_threshold <- 0.001
dcoloc_heatmap_effect_threshold <- 0.5
dcoloc_volcano_top_n <- 5

if (!contrast_column %in% colnames(pg_data[[]])) {
  stop(
    "Contrast column '", contrast_column, "' is not present in the Seurat object. ",
    "Available columns: ", paste(colnames(pg_data[[]]), collapse = ", ")
  )
}

available_conditions <- unique(as.character(pg_data[[]][[contrast_column]]))
if (
  length(reference_condition) != 1L ||
    is.na(reference_condition) ||
    !reference_condition %in% available_conditions
) {
  stop(
    "The reference condition '", reference_condition, "' is not present in ",
    contrast_column, ". Available values: ",
    paste(available_conditions, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

target_conditions_preview <- setdiff(available_conditions, reference_condition)
if (length(target_conditions_preview) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "No target conditions found in ", contrast_column,
    " after excluding reference_condition ('", reference_condition, "')."
  )
}

message(
  "Contrast column: ", contrast_column, "\n",
  "Reference condition: ", reference_condition, "\n",
  "Comparisons to run: ",
  paste(paste0(target_conditions_preview, "_vs_", reference_condition), collapse = ", ")
)
```

### Sample-level Aggregation

Per-sample means for the volcano side heatmaps. The Wilcoxon tests below still use every cell; these tables only show how the labeled markers look in each sample.

#### Abundance

In this section we calculate the mean CLR per sample × cell type × marker. The differential test in §5.1 does not use this table, only the heatmap next to each volcano shows the markers on a per-sample scale.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_aggregate_abundance
#| include: false

# Mean CLR per sample × cell type × marker. Used for volcano side heatmaps (§5.1.1).
summary_abundance_data <-
  names(markers_to_test) |>
  map(function(cell_type) {
    dat <- FetchData(
      subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == cell_type),
      vars = c(
        "sample_alias",
        contrast_column,
        as.character(unname(markers_to_test[[cell_type]]))
      ),
      layer = "data"
    )
    marker_cols <- setdiff(colnames(dat), c("sample_alias", contrast_column))
    dat |>
      pivot_longer(all_of(marker_cols), names_to = "marker", values_to = "clr") |>
      group_by(.data$sample_alias, .data[[contrast_column]], .data$marker) |>
      summarise(mean_clr = mean(clr, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
      mutate(group = cell_type)
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

# abundance_dir <- here::here("results", "05_statistical_testing", "abundance", "cell_level")
# dir.create(abundance_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# write_rds(summary_abundance_data, file.path(abundance_dir, "summary_abundance_data.rds"))
# write_csv(summary_abundance_data, file.path(abundance_dir, "summary_abundance_data.csv"))
```

#### Proximity

Similarly, build the per-sample proximity table once here, the same way as abundance above, so the clustering and colocalization plots (§§5.2.1, 5.3.1) show the same per-sample numbers in the heatmaps accompanying the volcano plots. We use the standard `FilterProximityScores()` function to drop marker pairs below an isotype-derived background, then `SummarizeProximityScores()` to take the mean `log2_ratio` per `sample_alias` × cell type.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_aggregate_proximity

# Mean log2_ratio per sample_alias × cell type × pair. The isotype cutoff is
# computed once on the full object: median isotype fraction + 2 MAD (minimum 0.001).
bg <- if ("isotype_fraction" %in% colnames(pg_data[[]])) {
  max(median(pg_data$isotype_fraction, na.rm = TRUE) + 2 * mad(pg_data$isotype_fraction, na.rm = TRUE), 0.001)
} else {
  0.001
}
summary_proximity_data <- names(markers_to_test) |>
  map(function(cell_type) {
    obj <- subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == cell_type)
    # Pull the markers out first. filter() is evaluated in DuckDB, and
    # markers_to_test[[cell_type]] is a list, which SQL cannot interpolate.
    markers_vec <- markers_to_test[[cell_type]]
    ProximityScores(obj, lazy = TRUE, meta_data_columns = "sample_alias", add_marker_proportions = TRUE) |>
      filter(marker_1 %in% markers_vec, marker_2 %in% markers_vec) |>
      FilterProximityScores(background_threshold_pct = bg) |>
      SummarizeProximityScores(
        proximity_metric = "log2_ratio", group_vars = "sample_alias",
        summary_stat = "mean", include_missing_obs = TRUE
      ) |>
      mutate(feature = paste(marker_1, marker_2, sep = "_"), group = cell_type)
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

#proximity_dir <- here::here("results", "05_statistical_testing", "proximity", "cell_level")
#dir.create(proximity_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
#write_rds(summary_proximity_data, file.path(proximity_dir, "summary_proximity_data.rds"))
#write_csv(summary_proximity_data, file.path(proximity_dir, "summary_proximity_data.csv"))
```

## 5.1. Differential abundance analysis

Differential abundance analysis identifies markers that exhibit statistically significant differences in expression levels between experimental conditions. This analysis is essential for understanding how experimental treatments, disease states, or other conditions affect protein expression patterns within specific cell types.

The analysis is performed separately for each annotated cell type, comparing marker abundance between a target condition (e.g., stimulated, treated) and a reference condition (e.g., resting, control). For each marker within each cell type, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (Mann-Whitney U) assesses whether the distribution of marker abundance differs between conditions. The Wilcoxon test is non-parametric, so it does not assume a normal distribution. That suits single-cell data, which is often skewed and highly variable.

The test compares marker expression values (CLR-normalized values) between cells in the target condition versus cells in the reference condition. For each marker, the analysis reports an effect size (the difference in mean or median expression) and a p-value. Multiple testing correction uses FDR within each cell type and contrast, not across all cell types together. Pooling cells this way ignores that cells from the same sample are not independent; use module 05b when replicates should be the unit of replication.

Results are organized by cell type and include both the raw statistical outputs and summary visualizations. Markers with significant differences (typically p_adj < 0.05) and large effect sizes are of particular biological interest, as they represent markers whose expression is substantially altered by the experimental condition. This analysis enables identification of condition-specific markers, understanding of cellular responses to treatments, and discovery of biomarkers associated with different experimental states.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_differential_abundance_analysis

differential_abundance_analysis <-
  names(markers_to_test) |>
  map(function(x) {
    tryCatch(
      {
        daa_res <- RunDAA(subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == x),
          contrast_column = contrast_column,
          reference = reference_condition,
          features = markers_to_test[[x]]
        )
        daa_res$group <- x
        daa_res$p_adj <- ave(daa_res$p, daa_res$target, daa_res$reference, FUN = \(p) p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"))
        return(daa_res)
      },
      error = function(e) {
        message(paste("Error for cell type:", x, ":", e))
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

abundance_dir <- here::here("results", "05_statistical_testing", "abundance", "cell_level")
dir.create(abundance_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_rds(differential_abundance_analysis, file.path(abundance_dir, "differential_abundance_analysis.rds"))
write_csv(differential_abundance_analysis, file.path(abundance_dir, "differential_abundance_analysis.csv"))
```

### 5.1.1. Summarizing plots

Here we create summarizing plots for the differential abundance analysis results:

1. **Per-cell-type volcano + sample heatmap**: For each cell type, a volcano (effect size vs −log10 adjusted p-value, top `daa_volcano_top_n` markers labeled by **adjusted significance**, not largest |effect|) and a row-z-scored heatmap of sample-mean CLR (`summary_abundance_data`) for those same labeled markers. Both are saved in the cell type's own folder.

2. **Effect-size heatmap**: Markers with `p_adj < daa_plot_p_adj_threshold` and `|effect| > daa_heatmap_effect_threshold` across cell types.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_differential_abundance_analysis_summarizing_plots

modality <- "abundance"
target <- setdiff(unique(differential_abundance_analysis$target), reference_condition)[1]

# results/05_statistical_testing/{modality}/cell_level/{target}_vs_{reference}/...
plot_path <- function(...) {
  here::here(
    "results/05_statistical_testing", modality, "cell_level",
    paste0(target, "_vs_", reference_condition),
    ...
  )
}

plot_data <- differential_abundance_analysis |>
  filter(target == !!target) |>
  mutate(neg_log10_p_adj = -log10(pmax(p_adj, min_p_value_threshold)))

# Per cell type: volcano with its n most significant labeled markers, plus a
# row-z-scored sample heatmap of those same markers' CLR means. Both saved
# under the cell type's own folder within the target-vs-reference folder.
walk(unique(plot_data$group), function(cell_type) {
  data <- filter(plot_data, group == cell_type)
  labels <- slice_max(data, order_by = neg_log10_p_adj, n = dabund_volcano_top_n, with_ties = FALSE)

  volcano <- ggplot(data, aes(difference, neg_log10_p_adj, color = difference)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = labels, aes(label = marker), size = 2.5, vjust = -0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
    scale_color_gradient2() +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")"), x = "Difference", y = "-log10(FDR-adjusted p-value)")
  export_plot(plot_path(cell_type, paste0("differential_", modality, "_volcano")), volcano, width = 6, height = 5)

  clr_mat <- summary_abundance_data |>
    filter(group == cell_type, marker %in% labels$marker) |>
    select(marker, sample_alias, mean_clr) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = sample_alias, values_from = mean_clr) |>
    column_to_rownames("marker") |>
    as.matrix()
  clr_mat <- t(scale(t(clr_mat[labels$marker, , drop = FALSE])))
  sample_hm <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
    clr_mat,
    color = PixelgenGradient(100, "BluesCherry"),
    name = "CLR z-score",
    main = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")")
  ) |>
    as.ggplot()
  export_plot(plot_path(cell_type, "sample_heatmap"), sample_hm, width = 6, height = 5)
})

# Effect-size heatmap of significant markers across cell types
heatmap_mat <- plot_data |>
  filter(p_adj < dabund_plot_p_adj_threshold, abs(difference) > dabund_heatmap_effect_threshold) |>
  select(marker, group, difference) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = difference, values_fill = 0) |>
  column_to_rownames("marker") |>
  as.matrix()
heatmap_plot <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
  heatmap_mat,
  color = PixelgenGradient(100, "BluesCherry"),
  main = paste0(target, " vs ", reference_condition)
) |>
  as.ggplot()
export_plot(plot_path("effect_size_heatmap_all_celltypes"), heatmap_plot, width = 6, height = 6)
``` 


## 5.2. Differential Clustering Analysis

Differential clustering analysis identifies markers that exhibit statistically significant differences in spatial clustering patterns between experimental conditions. In this context, "clustering" refers to the spatial aggregation of a marker with itself—that is, the extent to which a marker tends to form clusters or aggregates within cells rather than being uniformly distributed.

The analysis is performed separately for each cell type, comparing clustering patterns between target and reference conditions. A Wilcoxon rank-sum test assesses whether the distribution of clustering scores (log2 ratio of observed versus expected self-proximity) differs between conditions. Multiple testing correction uses FDR within each cell type and contrast.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_differential_clustering

differential_clustering_analysis <-
  names(markers_to_test) |>
  map(function(x) {
    tryCatch(
      {
        # Release the per-cell-type copy before the next iteration
        obj <- subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == x)
        res <- DifferentialProximityAnalysis(
          obj,
          contrast_column = contrast_column,
          reference = reference_condition,
          proximity_metric = "log2_ratio",
          metric_type = "self",
          method = "seurat",
          min_cells_per_group = 5L,
          diff_threshold = 0.01,
          min_pct = 0,
          min_diff_pct = -Inf,
          lazy = TRUE
        ) |>
          filter(
            marker_1 %in% markers_to_test[[x]],
            marker_2 %in% markers_to_test[[x]]
          )
        rm(obj)
        gc()
        if (nrow(res) == 0L) {
          return(NULL)
        }
        res$group <- x
        res$p_adj <- ave(res$p, res$target, res$reference, FUN = \(p) p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"))
        res
      },
      error = function(e) {
        message(paste("Error for cell type:", x, ":", e))
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

clustering_dir <- here::here("results", "05_statistical_testing", "clustering", "cell_level")
dir.create(clustering_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_rds(differential_clustering_analysis, file.path(clustering_dir, "differential_clustering_analysis.rds"))
write_csv(differential_clustering_analysis, file.path(clustering_dir, "differential_clustering_analysis.csv"))
```


### 5.2.1. Summarizing plots

Here we create summarizing plots for the differential clustering analysis results, with the same layout as §5.1.1:

1. **Per-cell-type volcano + sample heatmap**: Volcano of `diff_median` vs −log10 adjusted p-value, top `dclust_volcano_top_n` markers labeled by **adjusted significance**, beside a row-z-scored heatmap of sample-mean self-proximity (`log2_ratio`, `marker_1 == marker_2` in `summary_proximity_data`). Saved in the cell type's own folder.

2. **Effect-size heatmap**: Markers with `p_adj < dclust_plot_p_adj_threshold` and `|diff_median| > dclust_heatmap_effect_threshold` across cell types.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_differential_clustering_plots

modality <- "clustering"
target <- setdiff(unique(differential_clustering_analysis$target), reference_condition)[1]

# results/05_statistical_testing/{modality}/cell_level/{target}_vs_{reference}/...
plot_path <- function(...) {
  here::here(
    "results/05_statistical_testing", modality, "cell_level",
    paste0(target, "_vs_", reference_condition),
    ...
  )
}

# Self-proximity: marker_1 is the feature (marker_1 == marker_2).
plot_data <- differential_clustering_analysis |>
  filter(target == !!target) |>
  mutate(
    marker = marker_1,
    neg_log10_p_adj = -log10(pmax(p_adj, min_p_value_threshold))
  )

# Per cell type: volcano with its n most significant labeled markers, plus a
# row-z-scored sample heatmap of those markers' self-proximity. Both saved
# under the cell type's own folder within the target-vs-reference folder.
walk(unique(plot_data$group), function(cell_type) {
  data <- filter(plot_data, group == cell_type)
  labels <- slice_max(data, order_by = neg_log10_p_adj, n = dclust_volcano_top_n, with_ties = FALSE)

  volcano <- ggplot(data, aes(diff_median, neg_log10_p_adj, color = diff_median)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = labels, aes(label = marker), size = 2.5, vjust = -0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
    scale_color_gradient2() +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")"), x = "Difference", y = "-log10(FDR-adjusted p-value)")
  export_plot(plot_path(cell_type, paste0("differential_", modality, "_volcano")), volcano, width = 6, height = 5)

  prox_mat <- summary_proximity_data |>
    filter(group == cell_type, marker_1 == marker_2, marker_1 %in% labels$marker) |>
    select(marker = marker_1, sample_alias, mean_log2_ratio) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = sample_alias, values_from = mean_log2_ratio) |>
    column_to_rownames("marker") |>
    as.matrix()
  prox_mat <- t(scale(t(prox_mat[labels$marker, , drop = FALSE])))
  sample_hm <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
    prox_mat,
    color = PixelgenGradient(100, "BluesCherry"),
    name = "log2_ratio z-score",
    main = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")")
  ) |>
    as.ggplot()
  export_plot(plot_path(cell_type, "sample_heatmap"), sample_hm, width = 6, height = 5)
})

# Effect-size heatmap of significant markers across cell types
heatmap_mat <- plot_data |>
  filter(p_adj < dclust_plot_p_adj_threshold, abs(diff_median) > dclust_heatmap_effect_threshold) |>
  select(marker, group, diff_median) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = diff_median, values_fill = 0) |>
  column_to_rownames("marker") |>
  as.matrix()
heatmap_plot <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
  heatmap_mat,
  color = PixelgenGradient(100, "BluesCherry"),
  main = paste0(target, " vs ", reference_condition)
) |>
  as.ggplot()
export_plot(plot_path("effect_size_heatmap_all_celltypes"), heatmap_plot, width = 6, height = 6)
```

## 5.3. Differential Colocalization Analysis

Differential colocalization analysis identifies markers that exhibit statistically significant differences in spatial proximity patterns between experimental conditions. The analysis is performed separately for each cell type, comparing **cross-marker** pairs (`metric_type = "co"`) between target and reference conditions — self-proximity is tested in §5.2, not here. A Wilcoxon rank-sum test assesses whether the distribution of colocalization scores (log2 ratio of observed versus expected proximity) differs between conditions. Multiple testing correction uses FDR within each cell type and contrast.


```{r}
#| label: module05a_differential_colocalization

differential_colocalization_analysis <-
  names(markers_to_test) |>
  map(function(x) {
    tryCatch(
      {
        # Release the per-cell-type copy before the next iteration
        obj <- subset(pg_data, cell_annotation == x)
        res <- DifferentialProximityAnalysis(
          obj,
          contrast_column = contrast_column,
          reference = reference_condition,
          proximity_metric = "log2_ratio",
          metric_type = "co",
          method = "seurat",
          min_cells_per_group = 5L,
          diff_threshold = 0.01,
          min_pct = 0,
          min_diff_pct = -Inf,
          lazy = TRUE
        ) |>
          filter(
            marker_1 %in% markers_to_test[[x]],
            marker_2 %in% markers_to_test[[x]]
          )
        rm(obj)
        gc()
        if (nrow(res) == 0L) {
          return(NULL)
        }
        res$group <- x
        res$p_adj <- ave(res$p, res$target, res$reference, FUN = \(p) p.adjust(p, method = "fdr"))
        res
      },
      error = function(e) {
        message(paste("Error for cell type:", x, ":", e))
        return(NULL)
      }
    )
  }) |>
  bind_rows()

# Clean up memory
gc()

colocalization_dir <- here::here("results", "05_statistical_testing", "colocalization", "cell_level")
dir.create(colocalization_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_rds(differential_colocalization_analysis, file.path(colocalization_dir, "differential_colocalization_analysis.rds"))
write_csv(differential_colocalization_analysis, file.path(colocalization_dir, "differential_colocalization_analysis.csv"))
```

### 5.3.1. Summarizing plots

Here we create summarizing plots for the differential colocalization analysis results, with the same layout as §5.1.1. Each row is a marker pair (`marker_1__marker_2`):

1. **Per-cell-type volcano + sample heatmap**: Volcano of `diff_median` vs −log10 adjusted p-value, top `dcoloc_volcano_top_n` pairs labeled by **adjusted significance**, beside a row-z-scored heatmap of sample-mean pair `log2_ratio` (`summary_proximity_data`). Saved in the cell type's own folder.

2. **Effect-size heatmap**: Pairs with `p_adj < dcoloc_plot_p_adj_threshold` and `|diff_median| > dcoloc_heatmap_effect_threshold` across cell types.

```{r}
#| label: module05a_differential_colocalization_plots

modality <- "colocalization"
target <- setdiff(unique(differential_colocalization_analysis$target), reference_condition)[1]

# results/05_statistical_testing/{modality}/cell_level/{target}_vs_{reference}/...
plot_path <- function(...) {
  here::here(
    "results/05_statistical_testing", modality, "cell_level",
    paste0(target, "_vs_", reference_condition),
    ...
  )
}

# Cross-marker pairs. "A__B" matches summary_proximity_data$feature.
plot_data <- differential_colocalization_analysis |>
  filter(target == !!target) |>
  mutate(
    marker = paste(marker_1, marker_2, sep = "_"),
    neg_log10_p_adj = -log10(pmax(p_adj, min_p_value_threshold))
  )

# Per cell type: volcano with its n most significant labeled pairs, plus a
# row-z-scored sample heatmap of those pairs' log2_ratio. Both saved under
# the cell type's own folder within the target-vs-reference folder.
walk(unique(plot_data$group), function(cell_type) {
  data <- filter(plot_data, group == cell_type)
  labels <- slice_max(data, order_by = neg_log10_p_adj, n = dcoloc_volcano_top_n, with_ties = FALSE)

  volcano <- ggplot(data, aes(diff_median, neg_log10_p_adj, color = diff_median)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.7) +
    geom_text(data = labels, aes(label = marker), size = 2.5, vjust = -0.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
    scale_color_gradient2() +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(title = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")"), x = "Difference", y = "-log10(FDR-adjusted p-value)")
  export_plot(plot_path(cell_type, paste0("differential_", modality, "_volcano")), volcano, width = 6, height = 5)

  prox_mat <- summary_proximity_data |>
    filter(group == cell_type, feature %in% labels$marker) |>
    select(marker = feature, sample_alias, mean_log2_ratio) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = sample_alias, values_from = mean_log2_ratio) |>
    column_to_rownames("marker") |>
    as.matrix()
  prox_mat <- t(scale(t(prox_mat[labels$marker, , drop = FALSE])))
  sample_hm <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
    prox_mat,
    color = PixelgenGradient(100, "BluesCherry"),
    name = "log2_ratio z-score",
    main = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")")
  ) |>
    as.ggplot()
  export_plot(plot_path(cell_type, "sample_heatmap"), sample_hm, width = 6, height = 5)

  # Dot heatmap of diff_median for this cell type's significant pairs, dot
  # size = -log10(p_adj). ColocalizationHeatmap errors with fewer than two
  # significant pairs, so skip a cell type that has 0 or 1 instead of aborting.
  sig_pairs <- data |>
    filter(p_adj < dcoloc_plot_p_adj_threshold) |>
    arrange(desc(neg_log10_p_adj))
  if (nrow(sig_pairs) < 2) {
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  coloc_hm <- ColocalizationHeatmap(
    sig_pairs,
    marker1_col = "marker_1",
    marker2_col = "marker_2",
    value_col = "diff_median",
    type = "dots",
    colors = gradient_palette,
    size_col_transform = \(x) -log10(x)
  ) &
    labs(
      size = "-log10(p_adj)",
      fill = "Difference\nin medians",
      title = paste0(cell_type, " (", target, " vs ", reference_condition, ")")
    ) &
    scale_size(range = c(1, 5), limits = c(0, max(-log10(sig_pairs$p_adj))))
  plot_markers <- unique(c(sig_pairs$marker_1, sig_pairs$marker_2))
  export_plot(
    plot_path(cell_type, "colocalization_heatmap"),
    coloc_hm,
    width = max(4, length(plot_markers) * 0.15 + 1.5),
    height = max(4, length(plot_markers) * 0.15 + 3)
  )
})

# Effect-size heatmap of significant pairs across cell types
heatmap_mat <- plot_data |>
  filter(p_adj < dcoloc_plot_p_adj_threshold, abs(diff_median) > dcoloc_heatmap_effect_threshold) |>
  select(marker, group, diff_median) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = diff_median, values_fill = 0) |>
  column_to_rownames("marker") |>
  as.matrix()
heatmap_plot <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(
  heatmap_mat,
  color = PixelgenGradient(100, "BluesCherry"),
  main = paste0(target, " vs ", reference_condition)
) |>
  as.ggplot()
export_plot(plot_path("effect_size_heatmap_all_celltypes"), heatmap_plot, width = 6, height = 6)
```
